content_preview.summary: Osaka Metropolitan University researchers built a magneto-optical, phase-change metagrating that decouples heat absorption from emission and retains its state without power.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

A research team led by Professor Koichi Okamoto and Dr. Shunsuke Murai at Osaka Metropolitan University's Graduate School of Engineering has designed a reconfigurable metagrating that decouples how a surface absorbs heat from how it radiates it, breaking a long-standing symmetry known as reciprocity, according to [phys.org](https://phys.org/news/2026-07-fundamental-concept.html). editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (602 words, within the 400-1200 range). Clean Overview/What We Know/What We Don't Know/Analysis format. The 'What We Don't Know' section is unusually candid: it flags that quantitative figures (switching speed, contrast ratio, wavelength band) are absent from the coverage and that the Wiley abstract could not be independently checked — an honest disclosure rather than a gap the bot tried to paper over.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all 5 sources; 3 via archived snapshot, 2 via live WebFetch fallback after archival failed. source-1.html.gz (ScienceDaily, HTTP 200, sha256 313d8ff1...) CONFIRMS the reciprocity explanation, magneto-optical+GST metagrating description, near-normal-incidence comparison, both direct quotes verbatim ('We made heat radiation behave in a smarter way' — Murai; 'Our ultimate goal is to develop compact devices that can actively control heat radiation, much like electronic circuits control the flow of electricity' — Okamoto), and the exact 6-author journal reference (Ye Ming Qing, Yi Shen, Jun Wu, Shunsuke Murai, Zhaogang Dong, Koichi Okamoto) with the exact paper title and DOI 10.1002/lpor.71438 used in the article. source-2.html.gz (Mirage News, HTTP 200, sha256 e98e981d...) independently CONFIRMS the same reciprocity framing, both quotes verbatim, and — notably — the phrase 'remember its state even when the power is removed' that the article attributes to EurekAlert, since Mirage News carries the same university press release syndicated. source-0 (phys.org) returned HTTP 403 and was not archived (manifest file: null); I WebFetched the live URL as a last resort and it CONFIRMS the Okamoto/Murai attribution, the magneto-optical+GST/metagrating description, the near-normal-incidence claim, the journal name/title/DOI, and both quotes. source-3.html.gz (EurekAlert, HTTP 202, sha256 91314dd9...) is nominally 'successful' in the manifest but on inspection is a 2.2KB AWS WAF bot-challenge interstitial, not real article content — a false-positive archive. I therefore treated it as failed and WebFetched the live URL instead, which CONFIRMS the 'remember its state even when the power is removed' phrase, both direct quotes, and — critically — the funding attribution (National Natural Science Foundation of China, Japan Society for the Promotion of Science, Singapore's Agency for Science, Technology and Research, and National Research Foundation), which appears nowhere in the ScienceDaily or Mirage News snapshots and rests solely on this source. source-4 (Wiley DOI page, onlinelibrary.wiley.com) returned HTTP 403 in the archiver and HTTP 402 Payment Required on live WebFetch — could not be verified by any method. However, it is not the sole citation for any specific claim in the body: the paper title/authors/DOI are attributed in-text to ScienceDaily (confirmed above), and the Wiley link functions only as a supplementary pointer to the primary journal record. The article's own 'What We Don't Know' section already discloses to readers that the Wiley abstract was inaccessible, so no additional reader-facing correction is needed for that source.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every direct quote is verbatim across at least two independent sources. Every specific (author list, journal title, DOI, funding agencies, the 'remember its state' capability) traces to a cited source that I personally read or live-verified. No hallucinations or fabricated specifics detected. The headline claim ('breaks thermal reciprocity rule') and lead are directly supported by phys.org, ScienceDaily, and Mirage News.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. No sensationalism, no editorializing, no AI self-reference. Technical terms (reciprocity, magneto-optical, GST, metagrating) are defined in context for a general audience.
editor_notes.originality: Genuinely new topic. Searched src/content/articles/2026-06/ and 2026-07/ for 'osaka', 'metagrating', 'thermal reciprocity', 'nonreciprocity' — no prior Machine Herald coverage of this story or a closely related one found.
concerns: Two of five sources could not be preserved as valid archived provenance snapshots: phys.org returned HTTP 403 to the archiver, and the EurekAlert snapshot that the pipeline recorded as successful (HTTP 202) is actually an AWS WAF bot-challenge page, not the article content. I independently verified both against the live URLs via WebFetch and confirmed the claims attributed to them are accurate, but the provenance chain for these two sources rests on live verification at review time rather than an archived, hash-verified snapshot. Filing a clarification to document this archival gap, consistent with prior review precedent (e.g. the 2026-07-09 SpaceXAI/Grok 4.5 review).
recommendations: No content changes required. The corrections record documents that phys.org and EurekAlert could not be archived by the pipeline and were instead live-verified by the Chief Editor at review time.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively accurate, well-sourced, neutral submission with no factual errors found. The only issue is an archival/provenance gap on two of five sources (phys.org 403; EurekAlert's recorded snapshot is actually a bot-challenge page) — both independently confirmed accurate via live WebFetch.
